name: Tactile Push Button (6×6mm)
desc: The tiny click button that fits on a breadboard. Read it with INPUT_PULLUP, so no resistor is needed.
note: It has 4 legs in 2 connected pairs. Put it across the breadboard's middle gap and use legs on opposite sides.

name: Arcade Push Button (30mm)
desc: A big, satisfying arcade-style button with a microswitch. Makes any game controller or "big red button" feel real.
note: Use the COM and NO terminals (crimp or solder wires). Some include an LED that needs its own power.

name: Potentiometer 10kΩ (knob)
desc: A turnable knob that gives your board a value from 0 to max. Use it for volume, brightness, speed or game paddles.
note: Outer legs go to GND and VCC (3.3V on 3.3V boards!), and the middle leg goes to an analog pin.

name: Rotary Encoder with Button (KY-040)
desc: A knob that clicks around forever, with no start or end, and you can also push it. Perfect for menus and volume.

name: Analog Joystick (KY-023)
desc: A thumb stick like a game controller's, with X/Y directions plus a click button. Controls games, robots and cameras.
note: Power +5V from 3.3V on 3.3V boards. The button (SW) needs INPUT_PULLUP.

name: 4x4 Membrane Keypad
desc: A flat sticker keypad with 0–9, A–D, * and #. Use it for passwords, calculators and safes. It uses 8 pins.

name: TTP223 Capacitive Touch Button
desc: A touch-sensitive pad: tap it like a phone screen. It even works through thin plastic or paper.
note: By default the output goes HIGH while touched.

name: Slide Switch (SPDT)
desc: A small on/off slide switch. Use it as a mode selector or a battery power switch.

name: Tactile Button 12mm (with colored cap)
desc: A bigger, comfier click button with a colored cap. Same wiring as the 6mm one.

name: Push Button Module (KY-004 style)
desc: A button on a small board with 3 pins (S, +, −) and a built-in resistor.
note: Most modules output HIGH when pressed (pull-down on board). Check yours with the Serial Monitor.

name: Metal Push Button 16mm (with LED ring)
desc: A sturdy, satisfying metal button with a glowing ring. Perfect for big "launch" buttons.
note: The LED ring is a separate circuit. Check if yours is a 3–6V or 12V type.

name: Toggle Switch (SPST, low voltage)
desc: A flick switch with a satisfying click, for mode selection or a power switch.

name: 4-Position DIP Switch
desc: Four tiny slide switches in a row: set addresses or options at a glance.

name: 3x4 Membrane Keypad (phone style)
desc: A phone-style keypad: 0–9, * and #. Uses 7 pins.

name: 1x4 Membrane Keypad
desc: Four sticker buttons on a strip, with one common wire.

name: Slide Potentiometer 10kΩ
desc: A sliding knob like on a mixing desk: volume faders, game paddles, dimmers.
note: Outer pins to GND and VCC (3.3V on 3.3V boards), wiper to an analog pin.

name: Trimmer Potentiometer 10kΩ
desc: A tiny screwdriver-adjusted knob for settings you set once, like LCD contrast or sensor thresholds.

name: TTP229 16-Key Capacitive Touch Keypad
desc: A flat touch keypad with 16 pads: a piano, a calculator or a secret-code pad with no moving parts.
note: Out of the box it reads 8 keys; solder a jumper (TP2) to enable all 16.

name: MPR121 12-Channel Capacitive Touch (I2C)
desc: Turn 12 things into touch buttons: foil, fruit, conductive paint. Great for music projects.

warn.5: Most generic MPR121 boards are 3.3V only: power from 3.3V. With 5V boards, a level shifter on SDA/SCL is the safe choice.

name: Limit Switch (microswitch with lever)
desc: A lever switch that clicks when something touches it: robot bumpers and end stops.
note: Use COM and NO with INPUT_PULLUP.

name: EC11 Rotary Encoder (bare, with push)
desc: The knob part used in KY-040 modules, for soldering into your own boards and cases.
note: Needs pull-ups (INPUT_PULLUP) on A and B; middle pin to GND.

name: Arcade Joystick (8-way, microswitches)
desc: A real arcade stick with 4 microswitches. Build a fight stick or a retro game cabinet.
note: Each direction is a switch to GND: use 4 pins with INPUT_PULLUP.

name: Mechanical Keyboard Switch (Cherry MX style)
desc: The clicky switch from gaming keyboards. Add a keycap for the best-feeling macro buttons.

name: PS2-Style Wireless Controller + Receiver
desc: A full gamepad (sticks, d-pad, 16 buttons) for driving robots and playing your own games.
note: Uses the PS2X library (install from GitHub or Library Manager forks).

warn.5: Power the receiver from 3.3V. Its data lines often work with 5V boards, but a level shifter is the safe choice.
